summary: All 86 focused tests pass. The earlier model and malformed-count cases are covered. Object-only extraction still omits encoded credentials before evidence writes.
blocking_findings: RB4-01 high: src/storytime/book-pictures.ts:488-521,1171-1193 checks only brace-delimited objects. It does not decode JSON string layers or root arrays. Put an escaped credential in an object, JSON-stringify that object text, and place that string under an unknown review field. The outer object decodes, but its string value still contains escaped property quotes and Unicode escapes. secretFindings sees no credential, and jsonObjects cannot parse its escaped brace substring. The walker returns no finding. An encoded array string containing an escaped credential and an empty object also loses the credential element. Both provider paths then persist the raw answer and record success. Scan decoded JSON strings and arrays before object extraction discards their values. Preserve safe parser behavior and raw bytes. Add both-provider regression cases. This finding follows source inspection; no production reproduction ran.

Applicability: the actual phase diff adds provider execution, credential checks, evidence persistence, local serving, and the CLI wrapper. Task 9 changes the decoded check and its production callers. test-strategy.md:557-616 explicitly requires security review.
The task delta changes only src/storytime/book-pictures.ts, tests/storytime-book-pictures.test.ts, and the track plan. The Red tests remain unchanged after d1d58dcd.

RB3-01 closure for the reported cases: decodedAnswerFindings scans model values in complete decoded objects and embedded content objects. MiniMax calls it inside the paid callback at line 3341. T96 and T97 pass.

RA4-01 closure: the walker receives rawOutput rather than parseModelReview's filtered result. It scans malformed count keys, unknown fields, nested objects, and array elements inside extracted objects. T98 to T100 pass.

Selection and status coverage: the loop at line 1192 scans every extracted object. T102 passes earlier-object, later-object, nonzero-status, and directly embedded object-string cases. RB4-01 concerns values that extraction never returns.

RB4-01 extraction evidence: jsonObjects starts only at a left brace, at line 491. It passes only brace substrings to JSON.parse at line 514. It never parses a complete JSON array or JSON string value.

RB4-01 traversal evidence: each decoded string receives secretFindings and jsonObjects at lines 1175-1178. Unicode-escaped credential text remains invisible when an extra JSON string layer prevents object parsing. Array text exposes its object elements but not its escaped scalar strings.

RB4-01 persistence evidence: MiniMax records success at lines 1036-1043 after the incomplete callback check. It writes rawOutput and the review at lines 3384-3385. Kimi writes the review, raw copy, and success entry at lines 3702-3712. Both retain unchecked rawOutput. A safe review object can retain a PASS verdict in each proposed case.
RB4-01 is a source-derived finding. This audit ran no custom probe or new production reproduction. The source_derived_cases field supplies bounded synthetic cases for Green.

Write timing otherwise holds. MiniMax checks inside the paid callback before a success entry. Its refusal appends a sanitized failure entry. Kimi checks before its first record write. Its begin prompt and ledger already exist independently.

Kimi calls parseModelReview at line 3661 before the decoded check at line 3665. The check still receives the complete original rawOutput. Schema fallback therefore no longer removes its input. The comment incorrectly states that schema parsing follows the check.

Refusal messages at lines 3344-3345 and 3668-3669 use the exact shared suffix. Findings contain pattern names, not matched text. runPaidCall redacts and truncates propagated errors at lines 1052-1058. The production CLI boundary repeats redaction and the 500-character limit at scripts/storytime-book-pictures.ts:48-55,92-95. T88 and T103 pass.
Safe controls pass T101. MiniMax retains safe reported models from both envelopes. Kimi retains its declared model. Review rawOutput, raw copies, and Kimi source bytes remain byte-identical.

Robustness: JSON.parse yields acyclic trees. Object identity tracking prevents repeated visits to the same object, but separate decoding creates new identities. Finite decoded strings shrink through embedded object extraction. The walker has no explicit depth or work limit. Deep recursion or large extraction can exhaust resources. This audit established no resulting credential write. MiniMax's check remains inside the sanitized failure path; Kimi's checks precede record writes.

Parse errors inside jsonObjects are swallowed at lines 515-517. This preserves unclear-answer fallback, but the extractor can omit encoded values without refusing persistence. RB4-01 covers valid JSON string and array cases, not merely malformed input.

Kimi input checks retain the 65,536-byte limit, regular-file requirement, UTF-8 decoding, and NUL refusal at lines 982-996. MiniMax process buffering has no equivalent answer-size limit. This audit makes no availability assurance.

A2: No audited test changes a draft to a published artifact. Published camera evidence is a local capture mechanism. The specification excludes public release. Fictional character checks do not establish consent for a real named subject.

A6: The immutable measure/tracks.md has no security-resolved claim. Its phase diff is empty. The unrelated working registry changes remain outside scope. Green's log reports mutation results; this audit did not rerun mutations.

This task adds no database migration, authenticated endpoint, tenant boundary, or organization boundary. Provider execution still requires --paid unless --dry-run applies. The changed flow handles local provider text and evidence writes. It adds no shell interpolation or executable evaluation of decoded text.

source_derived_cases.name: quoted JSON object inside an unknown string value
source_derived_cases.construction: const secret = 'sk-' + 'SYNTHETIC'.repeat(4); const escaped = Array.from(secret, c => String.fromCharCode(92) + 'u' + c.charCodeAt(0).toString(16).padStart(4, '0')).join(''); const safe = { verdict: 'PASS', reason: 'The subject is visible.', observedCounts: { subject: 1 }, issues: [] }; const hidden = JSON.stringify({ value: secret }).replaceAll(secret, escaped); const raw = JSON.stringify({ ...safe, unknown: JSON.stringify(hidden) });
source_derived_cases.expected_after_remediation: Both providers refuse before evidence writes. MiniMax may append its sanitized failure entry. Kimi leaves its begin ledger unchanged.

source_derived_cases.name: encoded array inside an unknown string value
source_derived_cases.construction: Use the same secret, escaped, and safe values. const hidden = JSON.stringify([secret, {}]).replaceAll(secret, escaped); const raw = JSON.stringify({ ...safe, unknown: hidden });
source_derived_cases.expected_after_remediation: The shared walker decodes the array and checks its credential string element before either provider writes evidence.

source_derived_cases.name: root array with a safe review and an escaped credential string
source_derived_cases.construction: Use the same secret, escaped, and safe values. const raw = JSON.stringify([safe, secret]).replaceAll(secret, escaped);
source_derived_cases.expected_after_remediation: The shared walker checks every root array element before object selection or evidence writes.
